headline: MGS belly extends its rally as October CPI undershoots; the 5Y falls 2.2bp to 3.598% while the 10Y stalls
summary: Malaysian government bonds firmed again on Thursday, led by the front end and belly: on FAST's curve the 3Y fell 1.7bp to 3.401%, the 5Y 2.2bp to 3.598% (−4.9bp on the week) and the 10Y only 0.1bp to 3.841%, steepening 3s10s by 1.6bp to 44.0bp. The 10Y GII eased 0.7bp to 3.873%, 3.2bp over MGS. Hong Leong Bank's IRS closes as of Nov 18 were mixed (5Y +1bp to 3.60%, 10Y −4bp to 3.76%), leaving the 5Y swap spread at −2.0bp and the 10Y at −8.2bp, both near one-year lows. FX-swap implied ringgit yields (Nov 19, indicative) were 2.90% at 3 months and 3.02% at 1 year, 4.9bp and 2.6bp under the onshore curve, a gap that narrowed 0.6bp and 1.5bp on the day. Financial and SOE trading was light (15 trades), with government-guaranteed DanaInfra and TPSB paper 35–39bp over MGS; FAST's corporate curves were still dated Nov 18 at this run.
drivers: Belly bid on heavy volume; front end firms into the 3Y reopening

Buying carried over from Wednesday, when HLB counted RM6.91bn of govvies traded (+66%) and the GII share rose to 42%; today the 1Y and 3Y fell 1.7bp and the 5Y 2.2bp, so the RM5bn reopening of the 3Y MGS 3/29 met a firmer, not cheaper, market (the auction result was not yet published when this was written). AmBank argues bond prices have largely priced the next potential hikes. The 3s5s10s fly dropped 2.6bp to −4.6bp (20th percentile), so the belly is now rich to the wings.
CPI a touch below forecast; Q1 2027 hike still the consensus

October CPI rose 1.9% y/y against a 2.0% Reuters median (September 1.8%), with transport (4.2%) and electricity, gas and fuel (4.7%) the drivers and food easing to 1.7%. HSBC, ANZ and Kenanga still expect a 25bp OPR hike to 3.00% in Q1 2027 after the Q3 GDP beat, but the mild print helped the front end: the 3Y MGS is 65.1bp over the 2.75% OPR, down 1.7bp on the day (80th percentile, one-year average 48.1bp).
Treasuries rally on oil; ringgit steadies

The US 10Y fell 4.5bp to 5.064% at Wednesday's settlement as oil slid, despite Governor Waller calling for a 50bp December hike and hawkish Fed minutes; at the one-year daily beta of 0.15 that implies −0.7bp for the 10Y MGS, which fell 0.1bp, so the long end lagged and the belly did the work. BNM's reference rate put USD/MYR at 4.1106 (+0.12%, +0.74% on the week), though the ringgit closed firmer at 4.1100 at 6pm. The FX-swap gap to onshore narrowed only 0.5–1.5bp across 1M–1Y, too small to read on indicative quotes.
10Y IRS keeps falling; swap spreads near lows

On Hong Leong Bank's Nov 18 snapshot the 10Y IRS fell 4bp to 3.76% (−19bp in a month) while the 5Y rose 1bp to 3.60% and the 1Y 2bp to 3.63%, so the curve is 1s5s −3bp and 5s10s +16bp. The 10Y swap spread fell 2.8bp to −8.2bp (3rd percentile, one-year average +8.1bp), while the 5Y bounced 2.6bp to −2.0bp (1st percentile, average +10.3bp). These are one bank's indicative closes, and the 1–4bp daily moves are within its noise.
data: Slightly soft; transport and utility costs up, food easing. Keeps a Q1 2027 hike likely but not urgent.
A beat led by investment and E&E exports; it firmed Q1 2027 hike calls from HSBC and ANZ.
Held with a firmer tone; the Governor says incoming data decide any 2027 move.
Weaker long-end demand at a higher yield keeps a supply premium in 15–20Y.
MGS +RM4.7bn to a record RM238.2bn (33.1%); GII −RM1.3bn
Foreign demand for MGS remains the anchor for the belly and the 10Y.
Strong activity data fed the GDP upgrade.
First rise in four months; gives BNM room to smooth the ringgit.
view: Keep the modest belly long and stay neutral at 10Y: the 5Y overweight from 3.636% (Nov 17) is now 3.8bp in the money at 3.598% and stays open (target 3.55%, stop 3.72%), but with the 3s5s10s fly at −4.6bp (20th percentile) the easy part of the belly outperformance is done, and I expect the 10Y to hold 3.78–3.90% over the next two weeks. The pay-5Y-IRS-vs-long-5Y-MGS swap-spread trade from −4.6bp is 2.6bp in the money at −2.0bp (as of Nov 18; target +3bp, stop −12bp); I would not add a 10Y version yet, because the 10Y spread is still falling (−8.2bp, −18.7bp in a month) as receivers lean on the 10Y IRS. The FX swap still prices ringgit under onshore rates (3M implied 2.90%, gap −4.9bp; 1Y 3.02%, gap −2.6bp) and only about 15bp over the OPR at 3 months, so offshore money is not paying for an early hike while the 3Y MGS sits 65bp over the OPR: the front end is cheap to the swap market, but the 3Y did not cheapen into the reopening, so the 3.45% buy trigger was not reached and I keep it. The 10Y GII at 3.2bp over MGS (85th percentile) is 0.6bp in the money on the 'prefer GII' call (target 1.5bp, stop 6.5bp). In credit, SOE paper traded 50.0bp over MGS on average over five sessions against 75.7bp for financial issuers, and government-guaranteed names (DanaInfra 35.9bp, LPPSA 37.0bp) remain the cleaner value; the AAA and Cagamas 5Y entries are 2.2bp offside on the page, mostly because FAST's corporate curves still carry Nov 18 levels against today's lower MGS. Treasuries explain little: over four weeks the 10Y MGS is down 3.9bp while the US 10Y rose 11bp, a +3.5bp Treasury-linked part and −7.4bp local, and the daily flow signal sits at −0.50, on the sell-off line; its sell-off calls were right only 38.4% of the time since 2022 in an in-sample back-test, so I do not lean on it.

buckets.name: Front end 3Y vs OPR
buckets.stance: Neutral; buy only on a cheapening
buckets.why: The 3Y MGS is 3.401% (−1.7bp), 65.1bp over the 2.75% OPR, the 80th percentile of the past year (average 48.1bp). FX-swap implied 1M and 3M yields of 2.85% and 2.90% sit only 10–15bp over the OPR and 7.5bp / 4.9bp under onshore rates (gaps 0.5–0.6bp narrower on the day), so the swap market is not paying for an early hike. Nov 18 call (buy if the RM5bn reopening clears at 3.45% or above): not triggered, with the secondary 3Y at 3.40%.
buckets.call: Buy the 3Y MGS 3/29 at 3.45%; target 3.35%, stop 3.55%.

buckets.name: Belly 5Y
buckets.why: The 5Y fell 2.2bp to 3.598% (77th percentile, one-year average 3.445%) and leads the week (−4.9bp); the 3s5s10s fly is −4.6bp, 20th percentile (average −1.1bp), so the belly is rich to the wings. The 5Y swap spread was −2.0bp on Nov 18 (+2.6bp on the day), 1st percentile against a +10.3bp average. Nov 17 overweight from 3.636%: open, +3.8bp.
buckets.call: Keep the overweight: target 3.55%, stop 3.72%. Swap-spread trade (pay 5Y IRS vs long 5Y MGS) from −4.6bp: open at −2.0bp, target +3bp, stop −12bp.

buckets.name: 10Y outright
buckets.why: The 10Y is 3.841% (−0.1bp), the 78th percentile of the past year (average 3.670%, range 3.44–4.18%). It yields 122.9bp less than the US 10Y, near the tightest of the year; the 10Y swap spread fell to −8.2bp on Nov 18 (3rd percentile, average +8.1bp). Nov 18 buy level (3.90%) not reached.
buckets.call: Buy at 3.90%, target 3.80%, stop 3.97%; no position in the middle of the range.

buckets.name: Long end 10s30s
buckets.why: 10s30s is 49.7bp (+0.9bp), the 74th percentile (average 46.9bp), as the 30Y rose 0.8bp while the 15Y and 20Y fell 1.2bp and 0.9bp. The GII 7/40 cleared at 4.158% with a 2.32x cover, so long-end demand is still soft. Nov 18 neutral call unchanged.
buckets.call: Neutral; switch to flatteners after a long auction draws a cover above 2.5x.

buckets.name: GII vs MGS 10Y
buckets.why: The 10Y GII at 3.873% is 3.2bp over MGS (−0.6bp), the 85th percentile of the past year (average 1.0bp); the 5Y GII gap is 2.5bp, 98th percentile. GII took 42% of govvies trading on Nov 18 (HLB). Nov 18 call from 3.8bp: open, +0.6bp.
buckets.call: Prefer 10Y GII over MGS; target 1.5bp, stop 6.5bp.

buckets.name: AAA credit 5Y
buckets.why: FAST's AAA 5Y (4.114%, still dated Nov 18) is 51.6bp over today's 5Y MGS, a one-year high (average 28.0bp); like-for-like on Nov 18 it was 49.4bp, so most of today's widening is the MGS rally against a curve that has not updated. Nov 18 first slice at about 49bp: 2.2bp offside.
buckets.call: Add the rest at 55bp; target 40bp, stop 62bp.

buckets.name: Cagamas 5Y vs MGS
buckets.why: Cagamas 5Y at 4.000% (Nov 18) is 40.2bp over today's MGS, the top of its one-year range (average 22.5bp); Khazanah 5Y is 33.1bp over. Over five sessions, financial issuers traded 75.7bp over MGS on average (23 trades) and SOEs 50.0bp (40 trades; DanaInfra 35.9bp across 14). Nov 18 entry at about 38bp: 2.2bp offside.

watch: Next: the result of the RM5bn 3Y MGS 3/29 reopening (Nov 19), Malaysia's October trade data (due in the coming days after September's 54.5% export jump), US jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed survey (Nov 19 US) and November flash PMIs (Nov 20 US), then the Fed's Dec 8–9 meeting, where Governor Waller argues for a 50bp hike.
